title: Operating SSC on a real database: what the stub hid
summary: The store package ran its tests against test/NoSQLServer.cls, a stub that accepts every statement and stores nothing, and ooRexx resolves ::requires from the caller directory before REXX_PATH, so anything run from test/ silently gets the stub. On the real NoSQLServer v0.79 four behaviours matter.
invariants: Never qualify SSC persistence with test/NoSQLServer.cls; run live tests from test_live/ against a real backend.

NoSQLServer v0.79 UPDATE evaluates quoted literals as expressions: '3*4' is stored as 12 and '12-34' as -22. Put free text only through INSERT; UPDATE only ids (letters, _ and hex), statuses and numbers. SSC ids use '_' not '-'.
NoSQLServer v0.79 has no IN lists and keys join results by qualified names (r.object_id). Wrap the provider executor in SemanticSourceSqlCompatibility.
NoSQLServer v0.79 rewrites CRLF to LF on storage. SSC refuses such members rather than storing altered source; re-qualify on NoSQLServer v0.9x.
Install Crypto's Foreign Runtime provider (.CryptoForeignRuntimeInstaller~install) at the composition root: pure ooRexx SHA-256 is about 1.5 s per KB, Foreign Runtime about 0.5 ms.
Never name a variable RESULT: a bare message instruction (x~append(y)) sets RESULT to the message's return value.
